speaker_coverage_crosscheck.method: Extracted every 'speaker' field across story/structured_story/ch001.json..ch012.json and confirmed each resolves to a registered character's name/original_name/alias, allowing for compound tags (e.g. 'Hatter + March Hare') and case/article variants (e.g. 'King' -> CHAR-king-of-hearts alias 'the King').
speaker_coverage_crosscheck.result: All speaker tags accounted for. Remaining loose/compound tags after exact-string matching ('Alice's sister', 'CHORUS', 'CROWD', 'Cook', 'Duchess + cook + baby', 'King', 'Knave', 'Mouse', 'Queen', 'White Rabbit (acting as herald of the court, ch011)', 'another of the jurymen', 'another unnamed helper', 'cook + baby only', 'one of the jury', 'one of the jurymen', 'soldiers', 'the party (chorus)', 'unnamed crier/voice at the court', 'unnamed helpers') were manually verified to each resolve to an existing registered entry (CHAR-alice-sister, CHAR-crowd-ensemble, CHAR-cook, CHAR-duchess/CHAR-cook, CHAR-king-of-hearts, CHAR-knave-of-hearts, CHAR-mouse, CHAR-queen-of-hearts, CHAR-white-rabbit, CHAR-jury-ensemble, CHAR-crowd-ensemble, CHAR-card-soldiers-ensemble, CHAR-caucus-race-party-ensemble, CHAR-court-officers-ensemble); none is an unregistered character. 'the baby' (TERM-0039, the Duchess's baby that turns into a pig) is intentionally NOT registered here: it is a creature-transformation element (SUP-006) belonging to 04-creatures/creature's boundary, not a human-performer CHAR-*.
speaker_coverage_crosscheck.novel_parser_note: story/structured_story ch007.json and ch010.json carry a small number of 'UNKNOWN' speaker tags. These read as speaker-attribution gaps in 01-story/novel-parser's output rather than an actual unregistered character (the surrounding dialogue is clearly Hatter/March Hare/Dormouse tea-party banter and Gryphon/Mock Turtle/White-Rabbit-herald courtroom-approach banter respectively). Not registered as a character; flagged here for 01-story/novel-parser to review, per SOUL's rule that upstream speaker-attribution defects are reported, not silently patched downstream.

scope_decisions.decision: Excluded from the character registry: Mabel, Ada, William the Conqueror, Edwin and Morcar, Stigand, Edgar Atheling, Shakespeare, Father William, Elsie/Lacie/Tillie, Queen Victoria, Napoleon III, St Frideswide.
scope_decisions.reason: These are real-world/recitation/comparison names Alice or others mention in passing; none is ever depicted as an on-screen dream-figure or waking participant (each is explicitly noted in bible/dictionary.json as 'never appears on stage' / 'never appear outside the telling'). They remain adequately covered as plain terms in bible/dictionary.json. The one told-only exception, CHAR-tortoise, was registered anyway because bible/_index.json forward_refs_pending explicitly mandates that exact slug.

scope_decisions.decision: Dinah (Alice's real cat) is NOT registered in this file.
scope_decisions.reason: Per H1 SUP-002 and the WRITE_RULES.md prefix table, CHAR-* is for human-performer dream-figures and waking humans; Dinah is a real, on-screen animal and belongs to 04-creatures/creature's CRE-* namespace. CHAR-cheshire-cat carries a 'doubling' cross-reference note pointing at her (H1 ruling 5.3 B) without owning her registration.

scope_decisions.decision: The Duchess's baby (TERM-0039, later 'the pig-baby') is NOT registered in this file.
scope_decisions.reason: SUP-006 treats the baby-to-pig shift as a continuous-shot creature transformation, not a human-performer dream-figure; ownership sits with 04-creatures/creature. Flagged here only as a boundary note, not a defect, since no CHAR-* forward-ref for it exists in bible/_index.json.

defects_filed.summary: Two minor internal inconsistencies in the locked bible/dictionary.json: (a) TERM-0001 still calls Alice 'seven-year-old', pre-dating the H1-confirmed age of 'about ten' now recorded on CHAR-alice; (b) TERM-0025 (Dinah) cites 'the Cheshire Cat (TERM-0041)' but TERM-0041 is actually 'March Hare' (the correct Cheshire Cat term is TERM-0040). Neither affects the correctness of bible/characters/index.json, which used the correct H1-ruling values and the correct term id.
